title: Keep a record of every redemption

blocks.text: This practice continues the gift-card server: `src/main/java/com/example/practice/GiftCards.java` starts from the previous practice's solution.

Support settles disputes from the `redemption_log` table, and last month it couldn't: a cardholder complained about a redemption that was declined, and the table had no row for it. Write `Record`, marked `TODO`. It runs after `SendResponse`, and every redemption, approved or declined, gets one row through the given `insertRow`, with `COMMITTED` or `ABORTED` as its outcome.

Support must be able to find every row for a card number it is given, and a stolen copy of the table must not give card numbers away. The secret key in the field `key` is there for that, and `card_lookup` holds 64 lowercase hex characters. About 20 lines in total.
The tests run the whole chain in a real TransactionManager, with a database that allows three open connections at a time.

cases.says: an approved redemption gets one row with its last four digits, amount, response code and outcome
a declined redemption keeps its row, because the row is written on a connection of its own that the rollback doesn't reach
the lookup value is a keyed HMAC of the card number, the same for every redemption of the card
every connection the recorder borrows goes back to the pool, so later transactions still get one

origin.section: 9.6 A Decline Is Recorded Outside the Transaction That Rolls It Back

concepts: A transaction-log row is written on a connection of its own, from commit and abort of an abort participant after SendResponse, so a rollback doesn't erase the record of a decline.
A stored card number is found by an HMAC under a key kept outside the database; an unkeyed hash is reversed by hashing the few candidates that fit the known digits.
